text:
Maria (Support): FYI customer reported that some request IDs in their logs do not link to traces in the console. They see the request id but clicking it says \"no trace found\". Example request id: req-9f8a2c4b. Screenshot attached (linked in ticket).
Jon (Eng): Can you paste a couple of full request IDs + approximate timestamps? Is this across a specific service or region?
Maria (Support): Two examples from their logs: req-9f8a2c4b and req-4d3e1f99. Both from service `frontend-eu` between 2026-02-10T14:23:00Z and 14:27:00Z. Customer says this is intermittent, ~5% of requests.
Ryan (SRE): Initial hypothesis: either sampling/filtering at ingestion or the trace indexer dropped the last span batch. Any correlating ingestion alerts? @tracebot can you show recent ingestion errors for frontend-eu?
tracebot: ingestion-errors: 2026-02-10T14:22:00Z -> 14:30:00Z: spike in partial-span-write errors (50 errors, 0.8% of writes). Related error: \"KV_CACHE_WRITE_FAILURE: EPIPE\".
Jon (Eng): That lines up. Two possible root causes: (1) trace ingestion accepted root span but downstream child spans were truncated and indexing failed, leaving orphaned request IDs in logs, or (2) the request-id used by customer doesn't map to our trace parent header (different header name). Maria, did customer set X-Request-ID or traceparent?
Maria (Support): Customer says they use a custom header `x-cust-reqid`. We map `x-request-id` and `traceparent` by default. They forwarded full headers; I can repro with their header.
Jon (Eng): Ok that could be it — we only auto-link if header is one of the supported ones. Two quick checks: (A) run this curl to reproduce and check console linking, (B) check raw spans in ES for that request id.
Jon (Eng): Curl repro (use their header):
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.example/consume -H "x-cust-reqid: req-9f8a2c4b" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"q":"ping"}'
```
Maria (Support): I ran that against staging; console shows the request id in logs but no trace link. I then checked the raw-span index with this ES query (simplified):
```
GET /traces/_search
{"query": {"match": {"attributes.request_id": "req-9f8a2c4b"}}}
```
Maria (Support): No results. But searching for trace by trace id from the app (if any) returns a root span: trace-0a1b2c, but it has only 1 span and no child spans.
Ryan (SRE): That matches partial ingestion. deploy-bot: There was a rollout of trace-indexer v3.7.1 at 2026-02-10T14:20:12Z across eu-region. Some nodes reported EPIPE in logs during the rollout.
deploy-bot: rollout-link: https://ci.redwood/internal/deploys/8723
Jon (Eng): Action items: 1) Confirm header mapping logic — support runtime should accept `x-cust-reqid` via request header mapping config if set by customer. 2) Investigate trace-indexer error (EPIPE) and why it allowed root span but failed to persist children. 3) Backfill missing child spans if they exist in the ingestion queue.
Aisha (PM): Queue priority: customer is on Dedicated tier and this is affecting their SLOs. We should treat as Sev2. Please keep me updated with ETA.
Ryan (SRE): Quick repro steps for eng: tail the trace-indexer logs on node `indexer-eu-5` around 14:20-14:30; grep for EPIPE and partial-write messages. Also check Kafka consumer lag for span-child topic. Commands: `kubectl logs indexer-eu-5 -n redwood | grep -E "EPIPE|partial-spans"` and `kafka-consumer-groups --describe --group span-indexer`.
Jon (Eng): If we can reproduce failing to write child spans locally, add a guard that retries on EPIPE and ensures atomic write semantics so root/span linkage isn't left broken. I'll open a PR for a retry wrapper.
Maria (Support): Noted. I've told the customer we're investigating and will request they add `x-request-id` in addition to their header as a short-term workaround. They can also set up header mapping via support.
Ryan (SRE): After the rollout, we should run a script to find orphaned trace roots (root spans with span_count==1) and cross-check logs for request ids to relink. If child spans still exist in raw queue, we can reindex. I can run the initial query: `SELECT trace_id FROM traces WHERE span_count=1 AND timestamp >= '2026-02-10T14:00:00Z' AND timestamp <= '2026-02-10T15:00:00Z'` and join against logs.
Jon (Eng): I'll attach a small repro harness to the issue and start the retry PR. Ryan, if you find child spans in Kafka, coordinate reindexing.
Maria (Support): Thanks team. I'll collect requested logs and keep customer updated. :thumbsup:
